title: Island cell sync refuses symlinked stores before any prune or fill
action: Review B-P1-1 (transcript-proven): a repo committing .bee/cells (or .bee) as a SYMLINK defeats sync_worktree_cells' tracked-set shield - git tracks the symlink object, not paths under it, so the tracked set is empty and the prune deletes every *.json in the symlink's target (outside the store). Fix in registry.rs: before ANY prune or fill, check symlink_metadata on the island's .bee, the island's .bee/cells, the main store's cells source dir, and each archive dir the loop is about to enter; any symlink = the whole cell-sync is SKIPPED and the bootstrap report (map + text) names the symlinked path with a one-line reason - never followed, never deleted through (same D23 never-follow rule the knowledge walkers apply). Per-entry: DirEntry::file_type already does not follow; keep that. TDD red-first: fixture with .bee/cells as a symlink to a victim dir full of json files -> bootstrap leaves the victim untouched and reports the skip; a symlinked main-store source is likewise refused; the normal-directory path stays byte-identical (existing wsh/ips tests green).

truths: a symlinked island or source cells dir causes zero deletions and zero copies, with the skip named in the report
the transcript scenario (symlink to a victim dir) leaves the victim byte-identical

artifacts.substantive: symlink refusal plus tests, no TODO stubs

trace.outcome: sync_worktree_cells checks symlink_metadata on island .bee, .bee/cells, source cells, archive dirs before any prune/fill; symlink = whole sync skipped, named in report (CellsSync::Skipped); red-first proven against pre-fix code
